**Published online:**
2026-08-28

**Geographic focus:**
United States (North America)

**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical report [YES] — references recent PCE data, July policy meeting, past Fed communications
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — September rate hike probability, upcoming jobs report and CPI
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

**Synopsis:**
New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh spoke at Jackson Hole, striking a more hawkish tone than prior appearances but stopping short of explicit forward guidance on rate hikes. He signaled inflation remains too high, financial conditions are not restrictive, and rate hikes may be necessary. Markets repriced September hike odds sharply higher (35% → 57%). Investors welcomed the clarity on inflation intent but remain divided on whether a September hike is a certainty, with focus now shifting to August payrolls and CPI prints as the key catalysts.

---

**Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?**
Relevance: YES — covers Fed Chair speech, 2Y/30Y Treasury yields, S&P 500 reaction, USD, Fed funds futures pricing, and PCE inflation data.

**Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?**
Relevance: 85
Probability of increase: 57% (as cited from LSEG Fed funds futures at time of publication, up from 35% pre-speech)

**Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?**
Relevance: 30
Probability of holding: 43% (implied residual from futures pricing; some strategists explicitly cited uncertainty)

**Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?**
Relevance: 0
Probability of decrease: ~0% (no mention of cuts; narrative is entirely tightening-biased)

**Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?**
Sentiment: +65 — Warsh delivered a notably more hawkish tone than prior communications; 2Y yields hit a one-month high, September hike odds surged, and multiple strategists described the speech as hawkish. Uncertainty remains on the exact reaction function, preventing a fully committed hawkish read, but the directional bias is clearly toward tightening.
